ui.metaDescription: Why a real NV-diamond magnetometer measures with Ramsey interferometry instead of reading Rabi oscillations directly, and how the same coherence budget that limits entanglement in bell-state-explorer limits this measurement too.
ui.heading: Why Ramsey Interferometry
ui.subtitle: The Rabi visualizer shows a magnetometer's raw quantum wobble. A real device doesn't read that wobble directly — it runs a smarter two-pulse sequence called Ramsey interferometry. This page explains why, and how the same coherence budget that limits entanglement in bell-state-explorer limits this measurement too.
ui.toolboxCaption: This is a toolbox for exploring quantum-sensing concepts as intuitively as possible — hover or focus a visualizer to preview it here.

ramsey.label: Ramsey visualizer
ramsey.note: Like a vehicle sensing the terrain shift beneath it, the spin senses the field shift during free evolution — Ramsey interferometry at the quantum level.
ramsey.detail: Using a toy vehicle, observe the NV magnetic field detection detection sequence revealed on a Bloch sphere.
ramsey.spotlightCaption: The Ramsey pulse sequence and Bloch-sphere response as the vehicle crosses terrain — captured live from the Ramsey visualizer, not a rendered mockup.

rabi.label: Rabi & Zeeman visualizer
rabi.detail: A view of Rabi oscillations, phase accumulation, and fringe visibility. Here you drag a variable and watch the whole time-domain picture — the oscillation, the Bloch vector, the fringe pattern — respond continuously.
rabi.spotlightCaption: The Bloch vector precessing as the magnet auto-sweeps its full range — captured live from the Rabi visualizer, not a rendered mockup.

golf.label: Bloch golf
golf.note: An NV Single Qubit gate-navigation puzzle.
golf.detail: X, Y, and Z pulses rotate the spin toward a randomly placed target in as few strokes as par allows. Unlike the other two pages, nothing here is driven continuously or measured with noise — every move is an exact rotation.
golf.spotlightCaption: Every stroke is an exact rotation — X, Y, and Z pulses walking the spin to a randomly placed target — captured live from the Bloch golf visualizer, not a rendered mockup.
